statement: Radian measure theta equals arc length divided by radius.
180 degrees equals pi radians.
Arc length is r*theta when theta is measured in radians.
Sector area is r^2*theta/2 when theta is measured in radians.
On the unit circle, cos(theta) is the x-coordinate and sin(theta) is the y-coordinate.
tan(theta)=sin(theta)/cos(theta) when cos(theta) is nonzero.
sin, cos, and tan have exact values at integer multiples of pi/6 and pi/4.
The smallest positive zero of sin(x) is pi.
The smallest positive zero of cos(x) is pi/2.
The range of sin(x) is [-1,1].
The range of cos(x) is [-1,1].
tan(x) has vertical asymptotes at x=pi/2+k*pi for integers k.
A fundamental period is the smallest positive p such that f(x+p)=f(x) wherever both sides are defined.
The fundamental period of sin(x) is 2*pi.
The fundamental period of cos(x) is 2*pi.
The fundamental period of tan(x) is pi.
If g(x) has fundamental period T, then g(b*x+c) has fundamental period T/abs(b), for b != 0.
For A*sin(x) or A*cos(x), the amplitude is abs(A).
Multiplying a nonconstant sine or cosine function by a nonzero constant changes amplitude but not period.
Replacing x by x+c shifts the graph horizontally by -c.
Replacing x by x+c shifts the graph but does not change the period.
sin(x+pi/2)=cos(x).
cos(x-pi/2)=sin(x).
sin(x+y)=sin(x)*cos(y)+cos(x)*sin(y).
sin(x-y)=sin(x)*cos(y)-cos(x)*sin(y).
cos(x+y)=cos(x)*cos(y)-sin(x)*sin(y).
cos(x-y)=cos(x)*cos(y)+sin(x)*sin(y).
tan(x+y)=(tan(x)+tan(y))/(1-tan(x)*tan(y)) when defined.
tan(x-y)=(tan(x)-tan(y))/(1+tan(x)*tan(y)) when defined.
For y=A*sin(B*x+C)+D, period is 2*pi/abs(B) and midline is y=D.
For y=A*sin(B*x+C)+D, maximum is D+abs(A) and minimum is D-abs(A).
Simple equations sin(x)=a on 0<=x<2*pi can be solved using exact special-angle values.
Simple equations cos(x)=a on 0<=x<2*pi can be solved using exact special-angle values.
Simple equations tan(x)=a on 0<=x<2*pi can be solved using exact special-angle values and period pi.
Given two points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2), the midpoint is ((x1+x2)/2,(y1+y2)/2)
Two variables x and y are in direct proportion if y = kx for some constant k ≠ 0.
If x and y are in direct proportion, then y/x = k is constant for all nonzero x.
If x and y are in direct proportion (y = kx), then y = 0 when x = 0.
Two variables x and y are linearly related if their relationship is y = mx + b for constants m and b.
When linearly related variables (x, y) are graphed, they lie on a straight line.
For linearly related variables, the change in y is proportional to the change in x: Δy = m·Δx, where m is the constant rate of change.
Direct proportion is a special case of linear relation with b = 0: y = kx is linear with y = mx + b where m = k and b = 0.
An equation of the form y = mx + c, where m and c are constants, represents a straight line in the coordinate plane.
The slope (gradient) of y = mx + c is m, equal to (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁) for any two distinct points on the line.
If m > 0 the line rises left to right; if m < 0 it falls; if m = 0 it is horizontal.
The y-intercept of y = mx + c is the point (0, c).
The x-intercept of y = mx + c is the point (-c/m, 0), defined when m ≠ 0.
A line with slope m and y-intercept c has equation y = mx + c.
A line with slope m passing through point (x₁, y₁) has equation y - y₁ = m(x - x₁).
The slope of a line through two distinct points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁), then use point-slope form to find the equation.
A horizontal line through point (a, b) has equation y = b.
A vertical line through point (a, b) has equation x = a; it has undefined slope.
Two distinct lines are parallel if and only if they have equal slopes.
Two lines with slopes m₁ and m₂ are perpendicular if and only if m₁ × m₂ = -1.
A linear equation of the form ax = b has solution x = b/a, defined when a ≠ 0.
A linear equation of the form ax + b = c has solution x = (c - b)/a, defined when a ≠ 0.
A linear equation of the form ax + b = cx + d has solution x = (d - b)/(a - c), defined when a ≠ c.
A quadratic relationship between variables x and y has the form y = ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0.
For equally spaced x-values, if the second differences of the y-values are constant, the relationship is quadratic.
For equally spaced x-values, a quadratic relationship y = ax^2 + bx + c with a ≠ 0 has constant second differences that are non-zero.
The turning point of y = a(x−b)² + c is (b, c).
The axis of symmetry of y = a(x−b)² + c is x = b.
The x-intercepts of y = a(x−b)(x−c) are x = b and x = c.
The axis of symmetry of y = a(x−b)(x−c) is x = (b+c)/2.
The x-coordinate of the turning point of y = a(x−b)(x−c) is (b+c)/2.
The y-coordinate of the turning point of y = a(x−b)(x−c) is a((b+c)/2 − b)((b+c)/2 − c), which simplifies to −a(b−c)^2/4.
If a > 0, the parabola opens upward and the turning point is a minimum.
If a < 0, the parabola opens downward and the turning point is a maximum.
The solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0 are x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a.
The discriminant of ax² + bx + c is Δ = b² − 4ac.
If Δ > 0, the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has two distinct real solutions.
If Δ = 0, the equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 has exactly one real solution x = −b/(2a).
If Δ < 0, the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has no real solutions.
x² + bx = (x + b/2)² − (b/2)².
The y-intercept of y = ax² + bx + c is c.
The axis of symmetry of y = ax² + bx + c is x = −b/2a.
y is inversely proportional to x if y = k/x for some constant k ≠ 0; this applies for x ≠ 0.
The vertical asymptote of y = a/(x−b) is x = b.
The horizontal asymptote of y = a/(x−b) + d is y = d.
For y = x^n with n a positive even integer, as x → ∞, y → ∞ and as x → −∞, y → ∞.
For y = x^n with n a positive odd integer, as x → ∞, y → ∞ and as x → −∞, y → −∞.
y = 1/x has asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0; as x → ∞, y → 0⁺; as x → −∞, y → 0⁻.
y = x^(1/2) = √x is defined for x ≥ 0, passes through (0,0) and (1,1), and y → ∞ as x → ∞.
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of x with a non-zero coefficient.
The leading coefficient of a polynomial is the coefficient of the term with the highest power of x.
The coefficient of x^k in a polynomial is the constant multiplying the x^k term, and is zero if the term is absent.
(x−a)(x−b) = x² − (a+b)x + ab.
(x−a)² = x² − 2ax + a².
(px−a)(qx−b) = pqx² − (pb+qa)x + ab.
(x−a)(x−b)(x−c) = x³ − (a+b+c)x² + (ab+bc+ca)x − abc.
(x−a)³ = x³ − 3ax² + 3a²x − a³.
(x−a)²(x−b) = x³ − (2a+b)x² + (a²+2ab)x − a²b.
The x-coordinate of the stationary point of inflection of y = a(x−b)³ + c is b.
The y-coordinate of the stationary point of inflection of y = a(x−b)³ + c is c.
The x-intercepts of y = k(x−a)(x−b)(x−c) are x = a, x = b, and x = c.
For y = ax³ + bx² + cx + d with a > 0, as x → ∞, y → ∞.
For y = ax³ + bx² + cx + d with a > 0, as x → −∞, y → −∞.
For y = ax³ + bx² + cx + d with a < 0, as x → ∞, y → −∞.
For y = ax³ + bx² + cx + d with a < 0, as x → −∞, y → ∞.
(x−a) is a factor of polynomial p(x) if and only if p(a) = 0.
If (x−a) is a factor of a cubic p(x), then p(x) = (x−a)q(x) where q(x) is a quadratic polynomial.
If p(x) = (x−a)²(x−b), then p(x) = 0 has solutions x = a (repeated) and x = b.
The graph of x^2 + y^2 = r^2 is a circle with centre (0, 0) and radius r.
The graph of (x − a)^2 + (y − b)^2 = r^2 is a circle with centre (a, b) and radius r.
f(a) is the value of f(x) obtained by substituting x = a into the rule for f.
The graph of y = f(x) + a is the graph of y = f(x) shifted vertically by a units (up if a > 0, down if a < 0).
The graph of y = f(x+b) is the graph of y = f(x) shifted horizontally by −b units (right if −b > 0, left if −b < 0).
The graph of y = cf(x) is the graph of y = f(x) scaled vertically by a factor of c.
The graph of y = f(kx) is the graph of y = f(x) scaled horizontally by a factor of 1/k.
A combination is a selection of r objects from n distinct objects where order does not matter.
The number of combinations of r objects from n distinct objects is C(n,r) = n! / (r! * (n-r)!).
For combinations of r objects from n distinct objects, r must satisfy 0 <= r <= n.
C(n,0) = 1 for any non-negative integer n: there is exactly one way to choose nothing.
C(n,n) = 1 for any non-negative integer n: there is exactly one way to choose all objects.
C(n,r) = C(n, n-r) for 0 <= r <= n.
The expansion of (x+y)^n for positive integer n is the sum over r from 0 to n of (n choose r) * x^(n-r) * y^r.
In the expansion of (x+y)^n, the (r+1)th term corresponds to r = 0, 1, ..., n.
The numbers (n choose r) are called binomial coefficients because they are the coefficients of x^(n-r) * y^r in the expansion of (x+y)^n.
The n-th row of Pascal's triangle consists of the binomial coefficients (n choose r) for r = 0, 1, ..., n.
Each interior entry of Pascal's triangle is the sum of the two entries directly above it: (n choose r) = (n-1 choose r-1) + (n-1 choose r).
The sum of all entries in the n-th row of Pascal's triangle is 2^n.
An outcome is a single possible result of a chance experiment.
The sample space of a chance experiment is the set of all possible outcomes.
An event is a set of outcomes, that is, a subset of the sample space.
The complement of an event A, denoted A-bar or A', is the set of all outcomes in the sample space that are not in A.
The intersection of events A and B, denoted A ∩ B, is the set of outcomes that belong to both A and B.
The union of events A and B, denoted A ∪ B, is the set of outcomes that belong to A or B or both.
Two events A and B are mutually exclusive if they have no outcomes in common, that is, A ∩ B is the empty set.
The probability of an event is a number between 0 and 1 (inclusive) that measures the likelihood of that event occurring.
An event with probability 0 cannot occur.
An event with probability 1 is certain to occur.
The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.
An event is a subset of the sample space.
For equally likely outcomes, P(A) = (number of outcomes in A) / (total number of outcomes in the sample space).
P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersection B).
The relative frequency of an event, (number of times the event occurs)/(total number of observations), is a point estimate of the probability of that event.
The conditional probability of event A given event B is P(A|B) = P(A \cap B) / P(B), defined when P(B) > 0.
Events A and B are independent if and only if P(A|B) = P(A), provided P(B) > 0.
If A and B are independent, then P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B).
